inline_comments.comment: The `// @ts-ignore TODO: fix this` is suppressing a TypeScript error that is actually a fatal runtime bug. In the base file, `tooltipElem` is declared as `const tooltipElem = createTooltip()` (line 606). Reassigning a `const` variable throws `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable` at runtime in strict mode (which TypeScript class output uses by default). This means `setupToolTips` will throw every time it is called, completely breaking tooltip functionality. The `@ts-ignore` hides this from the compiler but does not prevent the crash. This needs to be redesigned — either refactor to avoid the reassignment, or rethink what this block is trying to accomplish.

Even if the `const` issue were resolved, this code unconditionally calls `select('body').append('div')` without first checking whether a `.mermaidTooltip` already exists. Every invocation of `setupToolTips` (including on diagram re-renders) will append a new tooltip `<div>` to `<body>`, accumulating stale, invisible elements in the DOM. Compare with the `classDb.ts` change in this same PR, which correctly guards creation with `if (tooltipElem.empty())`. The same guard is needed here.

Calling `.html(title.replace(/<br\/>/g, '
'))` sets raw, unsanitized HTML as tooltip content. If `title` contains user-controlled data or diagram-author-supplied text with embedded HTML/script tags, this is a cross-site scripting (XSS) vector. The existing `flowDb.ts` implementation correctly wraps the title in `DOMPurify.sanitize(title)` before passing it to `.html()`. The same sanitization must be applied here: `.html(DOMPurify.sanitize(title.replace(...)))`.

The inline styles hardcode `#ffffde` (background) and `#333` (border), bypassing the mermaid theme system. The CSS definitions in `flowchart/styles.ts` and `block/styles.ts` use theme-aware tokens — `${options.tertiaryColor}` and `${options.border2}` — so the tooltip respects the active theme (e.g. dark mode). With these hardcoded values, the class-diagram tooltip will always render as a yellow box with a dark border regardless of theme, inconsistent with the rest of the application.

Broadening the selector from `g.node` to all `<g>` elements that have a `title` attribute may attach mouseover/mouseout handlers to unintended structural SVG group elements (e.g., container groups, namespace wrappers, edge groups). This could trigger spurious tooltip popups for elements that were never intended to be interactive. Consider scoping the selector more precisely (e.g., `g.node, g.classGroup`) to match only the interactive node shapes used in class diagrams.

general_comments.comment: The same nine `.style(...)` declarations (position, text-align, max-width, padding, font-size, background, border, border-radius, pointer-events, z-index) are duplicated verbatim in both `classDb.ts` and `flowDb.ts`. A shared factory function — `createTooltip()` in `diagrams/common/svgDrawCommon.ts`, for example — already exists in this codebase and is the right place for this logic. Both files should call that shared helper instead of each embedding their own copy. This also ensures a single place to update if the tooltip styling needs to change.

The `// @ts-ignore TODO: fix this` comment in `flowDb.ts` should not be present in a submitted PR. If a TypeScript issue genuinely cannot be resolved at this time, `// @ts-expect-error` is preferred over `// @ts-ignore` (it will fail the build if the error is ever resolved, alerting maintainers to remove it), and the comment should describe *what* the error is and link to a tracking issue. As written, "TODO: fix this" provides no actionable information for a future reader.
